answer.text:
On startup, Paws walks every work item that was in flight (states `running`, `verifying`, `recovering`, `merge_queue`, plus `awaiting_input`) and decides, per item, whether to resume it, re-verify it, keep its merge-queue place, or ask in Linear whether to restart it.

The entry point is `recoverOnStartup` in `src/db/recovery.ts` (`src/db/recovery.ts:46-101`). Inside one immediate transaction it: (1) shifts runner leases forward so Paws downtime up to `offlineBudgetMs` does not count against an open runner lease [E1:44,52]; (2) lists all items in the startup states (`src/db/recovery.ts:53`, `src/db/recovery.ts:31-37`); and (3) for each item, decides and applies a `StartupDecision`.

The decision logic lives in `decideStartup` (`src/core/recovery.ts`) (`src/core/recovery.ts:84-106`):

1. **Merge queue** — an item waiting in the merge queue keeps its place (`keep_place`). The comment says its merge job first asks GitHub whether a merge call that may have been in flight went through [E4:79-80,96]. `mergeCallInFlight` reads the `merge_call` table for the item (`src/db/remote-merges.ts:78-80`). If the run was still active in the lane (cut short mid-work), the item re-verifies instead (`src/core/recovery.ts:94-95`).
2. **Merge was in progress** (per checkpoint) — re-verify (`src/core/recovery.ts:97`).
3. **Runner still holds the work** — a verifying item whose runner still holds its Closeout review re-verifies and attaches to that work (`src/core/recovery.ts:98`, `src/core/recovery.ts:81-82`); other states resume in a fresh session with `reattach: true`, reattaching to the same runner commands (`src/core/recovery.ts:99-100`).
4. **Crash-loop guard** — if the item was already resumed once (`recoveryAttempts >= 1`) and the previous resume is recent (`sinceResumeMs < RESUME_AGAIN_AFTER_MS`), it instead raises an `ask_restart` question in Linear (`src/core/recovery.ts:101-102`, `src/core/recovery.test.ts:82-109`).
5. **Otherwise** — a verifying item with a verification candidate re-verifies; everything else resumes once in a fresh session, from its checkpoint or, without one, from its branch (`src/core/recovery.ts:103-105`, `src/core/recovery.ts:76-78`).

Back in `recoverOnStartup`, a decision is only applied if nothing already enqueued covers it: skips include a parked capacity-wait job already pending [E1:62,103-114], a pending answer-resume, a pending transient retry (`src/db/recovery.ts:63-64`), and an existing pending process-restart resume (for `resume` with reattach) or open re-verify (for a verifying re-verify) (`src/db/recovery.ts:76-82`). Resumes are staggered: each resume is scheduled at 5-second spacing (`STARTUP_RESUME_SPACING_MS = 5_000`) so a restart doesn't fire everything at once [E1:55-56,85, E6:39]. `applyDecision` (`src/db/decisions.ts`) dispatches each type — `resume`, `reverify`, `keep_place`, `ask_restart` — to its apply function within the same transaction as the follow-up job (`src/db/decisions.ts:17-48`).

After the loop, `awaiting_input` items have their run capacity released, and if any open questions exist a `catchup` job (`startup-questions`) is enqueued once (`src/db/recovery.ts:89-98`).

The docs agree: "A restart is safe while work is running… Paws reattaches to the same commands after startup, including in-flight Closeout reviews and answer tasks" (`README.md:54`). A test fixture confirms items land in `recovering` after shutdown and are recovered by `recoverOnStartup` with staggered resume jobs (`test/startup-resume-stagger.test.ts:150-184`). Separately, `requeueOrphanedWork` re-queues in-flight items nothing is moving, failing closed a merge in progress into a re-verify (`src/db/recovery.ts:218-275`).

This is based on 19 source ranges in 16 files, and research stopped at the deep limit maxPasses, so other relevant code may not have been inspected.
